result.title: EEG-World: Context-Conditioned Dynamics of the Watching Brain
result.comment: 20 pages, 8 figures, 3 tables; appendix with 3 figures and 6 tables. Ancillary file lists the clip split
result.summary: Brain encoding models predict neural responses from audiovisual input, but typically overlook how ongoing brain activity shapes an individual's response. We introduce EEG-World, a recurrent world model that forecasts 10 seconds of EEG band-power dynamics from 6 seconds of preceding EEG and the subsequent audiovisual stimulus. Pretrained on continuous EEG, EEG-World learns shared neural dynamics and adapts to unseen individuals through lightweight subject-specific readouts. Using 2,584 hours of EEG from 78 participants, we show that nonlinear recurrent forecasting surpasses strong history-aware linear baselines at scale. EEG-World achieves a forecasting correlation of 0.261 versus 0.233 for the strongest history-and-video linear model, with a 3.3-second forecasting-horizon advantage. Its learned dynamics transfer to unseen participants, outperforming the linear baseline in 23 of 24 individuals after calibration. While ongoing EEG history accounts for most predictive performance, controlled stimulus analyses reveal an additional video-dependent component. This component also enables evaluation of visual representations, with V-JEPA 2 improving clip-locked prediction by 35% over combined CLIP and DINOv2 features. Our results demonstrate the value of transferable neural dynamics for individual EEG forecasting and highlight the importance of separating state-driven from stimulus-driven predictability.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EEG-World，以 6 秒历史脑电与随后视听刺激为条件，用循环世界模型预测 10 秒脑电频带功率动力学，并在 78 名被试、2,584 小时数据上验证其优于历史感知的线性基线及跨被试迁移。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文把预测能力显式拆为「状态驱动」与「刺激驱动」两部分，并据此比较 V-JEPA 2、CLIP、DINOv2 等视觉表征的贡献，这一分离思路可能为 LVR 中区分内部推理状态与视觉证据贡献、检验视觉旁路提供概念类比，可供核查。
